headline: 龐克佛朗明哥 Rocío Molina倫敦登台
context: 西班牙舞者 Rocío Molina 在倫敦薩德勒之井（Sadler's Wells）帶來新作《Calentamiento》，以龐克搖滾碰撞佛朗明哥，評論稱之為電力十足、令人無法預測。本週還有 Rhode Island 樂團 Downtown Boys 推出雙語政治龐克新專輯《Public Luxury》；Lyric Hammersmith 新劇《Relics》四兄妹為藝術珍品爭鬧。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Sadler’s Wells, London Molina says she wants a show that never finishes – this one is endlessly thrilling and surprising Rocío Molina has completely redefined what flamenco can be. Some purists say she’s not flamenco at all, and when, three quarters of the way through her latest piece, Calentamiento , she sits down at a drum kit and starts bashing out a 4/4 rock beat, maybe you would agree with them. But however crazy things get two hours in, everything is built on the pure craft of the flamenco dancer, and that’s where we start in this piece on the subject of beginnings. Calentamiento means warming up, which is what Molina is doing on stage before the audience has even sat down. She begins a footwork drill, a 12-beat phrase, the same one she has done since she was seven years old, she tells us. At 140bpm, she likes to start slowly (!), she says. Heels and toes hammer out the dancer’s daily ritual, the same way even the most prima of ballerinas starts each day back at the barre with a plié; the constant discipline of beginning again. sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: (Sub Pop) The Rhode Island five-piece return with a ferocious rallying call to fight for your beliefs, with bouncing basslines, muted house chords and stomping drums Optimism might feel outdated, but Downtown Boys are proud outliers. On Public Luxury, the Rhode Island band’s third and best album, they wear their politics proudly – while bringing new ambiguity, strangeness and shadow to their passionate, sax-blasted bilingual punk. Opener No Me Jodas (Don’t Fuck With Me) comes out roaring, fists up, but gives way to a bouncing, joyous bassline: a brutal, big-hearted reminder that there’s beauty in fighting for what you believe in. In the nine years since the band’s last record, they’ve served as public defenders and co-founded the United Musicians and Allied Workers union, and the five-piece sound muscled-up, reinvigorated, by this work. Viva La Rosa kicks off like dive-bar punk, before transforming into something grander, with soaring electric guitar and darkly beautiful lyrics: “Todavía creo en un future / Todavía veo nuestros muertos” (I still believe in a future / I still see our dead). sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Lyric Hammersmith, London Four siblings squabble over an art treasure possibly stolen by their grandfather in this riotous play by Ben Ockrent Ben Ockrent’s black comedy about a family in mourning has distinct strains of the ludicrous, though the cartoonish absurdities creep in gradually. But then families are ludicrous: badly behaved and falling into their early, childish roles, especially in extremis. The extreme situation here is not the recent death of a mother in itself, which has led four adult siblings to gather at her home and hash out matters of inheritance, but a single item passed down by their grandfather which brings them to blows. thread_text:
西班牙舞者 Rocío Molina 在倫敦跳出了搖滾味的佛朗明哥。

她的新作《Calentamiento》在薩德勒之井（Sadler's Wells）上演。一開場，她就在台上練那套她七歲起每天做的踢踏步——以 140bpm 「慢慢暖身」。到了演出後段，她坐上爵士鼓，打起 4/4 的搖滾節拍。純粹主義者或許會說這不是佛朗明哥；評論說這場演出電力十足，讓人不知道下一步會發生什麼。

同週還有幾件事。Rhode Island 五人組 Downtown Boys 推出第三張專輯《Public Luxury》，是帶西班牙語歌詞的政治龐克。Lyric Hammersmith 的新劇《Relics》，四兄妹圍著一件可能是祖父偷來的藝術珍品互相撕咬，評論說熱鬧好看。

—— 本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 6 月 26 日發佈的報導，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。

voice_text:
西班牙舞者 Rocío Molina 在倫敦薩德勒之井帶來新作，把龐克搖滾和佛朗明哥拼在一起。她從七歲就在練的踢踏步是開場，演出後段她坐上爵士鼓打搖滾節拍。評論說電力十足，完全不知道下一步是什麼。

同週另外兩件事。Rhode Island 樂團 Downtown Boys 推出帶西班牙語歌詞的政治龐克新專輯。Lyric Hammersmith 有部新舞台劇，四兄妹為一件可能是祖父偷來的藝術珍品爭得喧天，評論說好看。
